# The frame exchange of a live lib/pq parameterised call through the front
# door, paused at ReadyForQuery(I), followed by a Bind of the UNNAMED prepared
# statement with no new Parse.
#
# WHY IT IS HERE. lib/pq's query path, whenever the call carries an argument,
# prepares into the EMPTY statement name and then throws its own handle away:
# the only code in lib/pq that writes Close(S) is the statement's own Close
# method, which database/sql reaches only for statements obtained through
# Prepare -- and those are given generated NAMES. So nothing closes the unnamed
# one, and a lib/pq session is holding a live prepared statement at every idle
# boundary after its first parameterised query. Whether that session can be
# called "empty", and therefore moved or released by the scheduler, turns on
# that fact; and a client is entitled to bind that statement again without
# re-parsing it. The last four exchanges below are that entitlement, exercised.
#
# NOT REGENERATED BY THE TEST RUN. libpq_unnamed_statement_pg_test.go COMPARES
# against this file. Editing it is a deliberate statement that the front door's
# frame exchange changed; review it as one.
#
# WHAT IS REDACTED, AND WHY. The credential in the PasswordMessage is never
# written down. ParameterStatus values are the target server's own -- its
# version string, its time zone, its float digits -- so recording them would
# make this file fail on the next PostgreSQL build; that those values are
# relayed faithfully is asserted by the startup GUC cells instead. The backend
# key data varies per connection.
#
# The ParameterStatus NAMES are not redacted, and they do depend on the target
# server's build: a PostgreSQL upgrade that reports a new parameter changes this
# list, and the fix is to re-read the exchange and edit this file.
#
# HOW THE FRAMES WERE SEEN. The front door has no plaintext path, so a tap
# between the driver and the listener would see ciphertext. The test puts a
# local relay in front instead: lib/pq connects to it in the clear, it speaks
# TLS to the real listener, and it forwards whole frames in both directions.
# When the driver goes idle the test stops the relay and keeps the SAME
# authenticated connection, so the final Bind lands in the session lib/pq
# opened, holding the statement lib/pq parsed.

## session-open
driver -> front door  Startup(3.0) client_encoding=UTF8 database=pgtarget datestyle=ISO, MDY user=root
front door -> driver  Authentication(3)
driver -> front door  PasswordMessage (redacted)
front door -> driver  Authentication(0)
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus DateStyle=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus IntervalStyle=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus TimeZone=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus application_name=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus client_encoding=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus default_transaction_read_only=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus in_hot_standby=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus integer_datetimes=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus is_superuser=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus scram_iterations=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus server_encoding=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus server_version=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus session_authorization=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus standard_conforming_strings=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus application_name=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus is_superuser=<value>
front door -> driver  ParameterStatus session_authorization=<value>
front door -> driver  BackendKeyData (pid and secret vary per connection)
front door -> driver  ReadyForQuery 'I'

## the driver's own preparation -- into the EMPTY name, and never closed
driver -> front door  Parse statement="" query="SELECT $1::int + 1" param-oids=[]
driver -> front door  Describe kind='S' name=""
driver -> front door  Sync
front door -> driver  ParseComplete
front door -> driver  ParameterDescription oids=[23]
front door -> driver  RowDescription ?column?:oid=23:fmt=0
front door -> driver  ReadyForQuery 'I'

## the driver's own execution -- 41 in, 42 out, and lib/pq asked for binary
driver -> front door  Bind portal="" statement="" params="41"/fmt=0 result-formats=[1]
driver -> front door  Execute portal="" max-rows=0
driver -> front door  Sync
front door -> driver  BindComplete
front door -> driver  DataRow "\x00\x00\x00*"
front door -> driver  CommandComplete "SELECT 1"
front door -> driver  ReadyForQuery 'I'

## THE PROOF: a Bind of the unnamed statement with NO new Parse.
##
## The parameter is 100 rather than 41 so the answer cannot have come from
## anything cached: 101 can only have been produced by re-executing the
## statement at the target with the new value. There is no ErrorResponse here,
## and in particular no 26000 -- the front door did not tell the client it had
## never parsed a statement it had parsed.
driver -> front door  Bind portal="" statement="" params="100"/fmt=0 result-formats=[0]
driver -> front door  Execute portal="" max-rows=0
driver -> front door  Sync
front door -> driver  BindComplete
front door -> driver  DataRow "101"
front door -> driver  CommandComplete "SELECT 1"
front door -> driver  ReadyForQuery 'I'

# CONTROLS RUN AGAINST THIS EXCHANGE, 2026-09-16, against the live PostgreSQL
# the test skips without.
#
# A green cell is evidence only if it can go red, and these say what turns it.
# Neither mutation is committed; both were applied, run, and reverted.
#
# 1. THE FRONT DOOR'S STORE. Adding `s.ext.dropUnnamed()` beside the existing
#    `s.ext.dropAllPortals()` in core/exec/wire_extended.go's Sync handling --
#    that is, destroying the unnamed statement at every idle boundary instead of
#    only on the simple-query path -- reddens the cell before it even reaches
#    the final Bind: the DRIVER's own query fails with
#      pq: exec: prepared statement does not exist (26000)
#    because lib/pq's own preparation ends in a Sync too, and its Bind then
#    names a statement the store has just forgotten. That is the shape of the
#    defect this exchange exists to catch, and it is worth recording that it
#    breaks a real driver one frame earlier than expected.
#
# 2. THE OBSERVATION. The first mutation proves the store matters; it does not
#    prove the cell's refusal arm is live, because the cell never got that far.
#    So the injected Bind's statement name was changed from "" to a name never
#    parsed, and the cell fails there, reporting
#      ERROR 26000: exec: prepared statement does not exist (gate/unknown-statement)
#    -- the front door's own manufactured refusal, which is exactly what the
#    assertion is watching for. The arm is executed and it reddens.
#
# The paired cell in libpq_unnamed_statement_pg_test.go covers the other
# direction: after the client explicitly Closes the unnamed statement, a Bind of
# it MUST be refused with 26000 and the session must survive. Without that, this
# artifact would also be satisfied by a front door that tracked no statement
# lifetime at all and forwarded every Bind blindly.
